header_and_summary:
Date: 2026-07-04
Start: 16:00 UTC | Duration: 58 minutes
Attendees: Redwood (Aisha, Diego, Mina) + Northwind Logistics (Tom, Priya, Ethan, Marta, Samir)

Summary: Implementation kickstart for Northwind's platform integration with Redwood Inference private/staging environment. Primary goals: agree runbook, confirm network & security prerequisites (VPC peering, KMS), decide hosting profile for pilot (hosted vs dedicated switchover path), and schedule VPC walkthrough and pilot start date.

Topics covered: Rollout timeline, staging vs prod differences, data residency and encryption, SSO/SAML onboarding, observability and cost guardrails, resource sizing and autoscaling policy for initial pilot.

Action items captured (see action_items field).
transcript:
[00:00] Aisha (Redwood): OK good afternoon everyone, thanks for carving out time today. this is the implementation kickstart, we want to walk through the runbook and make sure we have the network and security items covered before the pilot.
[00:18] Tom (Northwind): Yeah thanks, appreciate it. we've been looking at the docs, there's a few places where we need clarity on the VPC and the logging setup.
[00:28] Mina (Redwood CSM): quick note — I'll be running the weekly syncs and keeping the onboarding timeline, but Diego will own the staging deployment details.
[00:36] Diego (Redwood SE): hi all, I'll jump in on infra and runtime pieces, happy to go deep on kernels / quantization later.
[00:44] Priya (Platform Eng): big picture — Northwind wants predictable latency for our route optimization API, plus strict data residency. we can't send route telemetry outside EU.
[00:58] Aisha: got it. when you say predictable latency, what are the 95th pct targets you're thinking?
[01:06] Tom: ideally under 120ms for short prompts, and sub-300ms for longer sessions — this is tough but it's our threshold for user-facing features.
[01:18] Diego: for the pilot we can size a dedicated pool with pinned model version to hit those SLOs; there's tradeoffs versus hosted — cost goes up with dedicated.
[01:30] Tom: yeah we're aware of cost. we want a proof that latency meets SLA before committing to reserved capacity.
[01:36] Marta (Product): timeline — we want pilot data in two weeks and go/no-go decision three weeks out.
[01:44] Mina: that's doable if network prep and secrets access happen this week.
[01:50] Priya: question about private deployment — do we need full on-prem nodes or VPC peering? we prefer VPC peering to avoid hardware procurement.
[02:02] Diego: VPC peering or PrivateLink equivalent is our recommendation for EU; on-prem package is also possible but slower. for now we'll do a VPC peering path into our staging cluster in eu-west-1.
[02:16] Ethan (Security): what about encryption at rest and KMS? we use an HSM-backed KMS and need audit logs.
[02:24] Aisha: Redwood Private integrates with customer KMS via KMIP or cloud KMS keys, and we ship audit logs to your SIEM. We'll share the security integrations doc.
[02:36] Tom: can you send the SOC2 and ISO attestation? we need to start security review.
[02:42] Mina: yes, we'll attach SOC 2 Type II and our security whitepaper; Diego will give a detailed list of logs and log formats.
[02:50] [brief crosstalk] Samir: sorry, quick ops question — how does autoscaling behave for burst traffic?
[02:58] Diego: autoscaling is policy-based; for the dedicated pilot we'll set a burst buffer and fallback to smaller quantized model variants when capacity is low. for real-time SLOs we use continuous batching to keep latency stable.
[03:12] Priya: small nit — earlier docs mentioned "KV cahce" — is that KV cache?
[03:18] Diego: yes it's KV cache, sorry bad transcription in the docs; it's the KV store for transformer caches.
[03:24] Tom: we'll need details on model pinning and rollout — how do rollbacks work if a new model regresses?
[03:32] Aisha: rollouts can be canaryed by percentage or route; automatic fallback is configured so if latency or quality drops we revert. we'll include the rollback playbook in the runbook.
[03:44] Marta: on observability — what dashboards will we get out of the box? token-level cost, latencies per route, error traces?
[03:52] Mina: yes, Redwood Console gives per-route latency, token costs, traces and error histograms. we can set up a shared dashboard for your team.
[04:02] Ethan: SSO is a blocker — we need SAML/SSO for access controls and RBAC tied into our identity provider.
[04:10] Aisha: SAML SSO and SCIM provisioning supported; we'll need an admin to configure SSO and mapping. Mina can coordinate.
[04:20] Priya: there's also network egress restrictions — firewall rules only allow a few CIDRs to talk out. We'll send the exact CIDRs.
[04:28] Diego: perfect. for the pilot we'll provide a small set of IPs for staging. if you have NAT boxes we'll work through routes.
[04:36] [10 minute mark summary paraphrase omitted]
[10:20] Tom: security review will want details on log retention and PII handling — what retention policies are applied in staging?
[10:30] Diego: staging mirrors prod for log retention by default, but you can change retention windows and redact fields before logs ship to your SIEM.
[10:40] Ethan: do you support field-level encryption so PII never leaves our control?
[10:46] Aisha: we support tokenization and envelope encryption patterns; also customer-managed keys so data at rest is under your KMS. we'll surface patterns in the runbook.
[11:00] Marta: ok timeline recap, pilot start 2026-07-13, 2 week run, decision by 2026-07-27.
[11:08] Mina: I'll create the calendar invites and weekly agenda.
[11:12] Priya: network team availability — we can do the peer walkthrough next Thursday.
[11:18] Diego: I'll prepare a network checklist and a Terraform reference for the peering TF module.
[11:24] Tom: curious about cost controls — can you limit token spend per route?
[11:30] Aisha: yes, per-route quotas and token caps are supported; we can gate routes and set alerts for spend.
[11:38] Samir: we want a fail-open or fail-closed behavior for network failures?
[11:44] Diego: recommend fail-closed for user-facing workflows; fail-open maybe for low-risk analytics jobs. we'll document recommended policies.
[12:00] [short pause]
[12:08] Priya: question about model variants — how do you handle quantized models, does that change latency characteristics significantly?
[12:16] Diego: quantized models reduce memory and cost, sometimes with small quality deltas. for the pilot we can test both full fp16 and 4-bit quantized variants and show comparative latency/cost numbers.
[12:30] Tom: can you run a tiny benchmark with our sample prompt set?
[12:34] Aisha: yes, Diego will take the prompt set and run it in staging; send the prompts after the call.
[12:40] Marta: who will be the primary contact for day-to-day?
[12:44] Mina: that'll be me for onboarding and Aisha for commercial items; Diego for technical escalations.
[12:50] Ethan: compliance question — do you provide audit logs with user identifiers for who called an endpoint?
[12:58] Diego: yes, token-level attribution and API key accounting are in audit logs, they include calling principal, route, model version and response time.
[13:06] Tom: how do you handle data residency if a model cache stores prefixes that could be sensitive?
[13:14] Aisha: prefix/KV caching can be disabled or limited; we recommend limiting TTL and using encryption on cached items. we'll put best-practices in the runbook.
[13:28] [20 minute mark — misc small talk]
[21:10] Priya: Ops — what's the expected cloud footprint during pilot? GPU type, approx number of GPUs?
[21:18] Diego: for latency targets you mentioned, two A100-class or one H100 equiv in ded queue for initial pilot. we'll provide a sizing estimate doc.
[21:28] Samir: are there known network requirements for gRPC vs REST?
[21:34] Diego: both OK; gRPC has some perf benefits but REST is simpler for your stack. we'll include examples.
[21:44] Tom: procurement and legal — we'll need an MSA to review.
[21:50] Aisha: legal will send the standard MSA and security addendum, we'll mark it as priority.
[21:56] Priya: any gotchas with VPC peering and cross-account routing?
[22:02] Diego: cross-account peering requires routes set on both sides and sometimes Transit Gateway for complex topologies; we'll include diagrams.
[22:10] Ethan: can we run a security scan on a staging node image?
[22:16] Aisha: yes you can run scans; we also provide hardened images as part of the package.
[22:24] [30 minute marker — longer technical dive]
[30:02] Diego: here's a short rundown of the runbook sections — pre-flight (network, keys, SSO), staging deploy (helm charts, manifests), validation (latency, quality evals), pilot ops (alerts, runbooks), and rollback.
[30:20] Priya: in pre-flight we need the exact ports and IPs, plus NAT behavior — please provide.
[30:28] Diego: noted. we'll include a table of endpoints and ports.
[30:34] Tom: re: evaluation — we want pass/fail criteria for quality regressions.
[30:40] Mina: we'll pair on an eval set you provide; Redwood Optimize can run regression alerts against that test set.
[30:50] Marta: do we get to see cost estimates per call and per-route?
[30:56] Aisha: yes, Console shows token-level breakdown and per-route cost. we'll share the cost model used for the quote.
[31:04] Samir: ops — what about incident response SLAs?
[31:10] Mina: for pilot we'll have 24/7 Slack escalation to on-call, production SLAs are part of the dedicated contract.
[31:18] Tom: any blockers we should be aware of?
[31:22] Diego: none technical beyond the network and SSO; procurement/contracting can slow timeline.
[31:28] [small laughter]
[31:34] Priya: we'll prioritize network diagrams this week.
[31:36] Aisha: great. Diego, can you outline the minimal terraform or helm bits we need?
[31:42] Diego: sure — I'll drop a small repo with examples: k8s Service/Ingress, secrets setup pointing at KMS, and a sample TF module for peering.
[31:52] Priya: that repo will be helpful.
[31:56] Tom: let's talk about rollback thresholds — if latency degrades by 20% or error rate > 1% we revert?
[32:04] Diego: those thresholds are reasonable for pilot; we'll instrument and tune.
[32:10] Ethan: for audit purposes we need signed logs for three months.
[32:16] Aisha: we can export logs to your archive bucket and TTL them per policy.
[32:22] [40 minute mark — administrative wrap-up items]
[40:00] Mina: quick checklist: runbook draft, network diagram, SAML details, KMS requirements, prompts for benchmarking. Everyone OK with this list?
[40:08] Priya: yes.
[40:10] Tom: yes.
[40:12] Marta: yes.
[40:14] Ethan: yes.
[40:16] Samir: yes.
[40:18] Aisha: I'll share the runbook and pricing worksheet by Monday.
[40:24] Diego: I'll ship the staging playbook and sample manifests by Wednesday.
[40:30] Mina: I'll schedule the recurring pilot sync and add the VPC walkthrough invite.
[40:36] [short side conversation about calendar times]
[46:02] Tom: one last thought — if we find cost too high, is there a path to hybrid mode where some routes go to hosted while critical routes stay private?
[46:12] Aisha: yes hybrid routing is supported — route rules can send non-sensitive calls to hosted catalog models and sensitive calls to your private pool.
[46:22] Priya: can we test hybrid routing during the pilot?
[46:28] Diego: yes, configure routes in the staging Console. we'll show you during the pilot.
[46:36] Tom: thanks everyone, this was helpful.
[46:40] Aisha: recap — next week VPC walkthrough, runbook by Monday, staging manifests mid-week, pilot start 2026-07-13.
[46:52] Mina: action items in the chat; I'll follow up with an invite and notes.
[47:00] [closing brief idle chatter and goodbyes]
[57:45] END OF CALL

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-typed product names (e.g., Redwood Dedicate) in automated docs — confirm spelling in shared runbook. The transcript may miss short interruptions.
